title: Q-BUDGET-SURFACES: put the dashboard console agent and the site worker under the spend governor
body:
**Owner:** operations
**Trigger:** executor tick, driver order
**Done check:** grep:dashboard/worker.js::budgetEnv(env, SHARES.dashboard)
**Status:** closed

SPEND-GOVERNOR-1 (seed/worker/src/budget.js) meters and caps every model call of the tick worker. The dashboard's console agent (dashboard/agent.js, Workers AI on each owner request) and the site worker (site/worker.js, AI binding) draw on the same account's Workers AI allowance but are not metered, so their use is invisible to the governor and can push the account past the owner's budget.

Acceptance: both workers call Workers AI only through governedAI with a ledger the tick governor reads (one shared budget_ledger in the org D1, or a per-worker share of the day's allowance declared in the instance manifest); a frozen budget makes the console answer from its rule-based digest without a model; the site keeps serving pages with no model call.

Test plan: dashboard/test and site tests cover a frozen budget (no AI.run call) and a lean budget (one call per request).

size: S

**Closing probe:** `grep:dashboard/worker.js::budgetEnv(env, SHARES.dashboard)` and `grep:site/worker.js::budgetEnv(env, SHARES.site)`

**Evidence:** both workers already wrapped env in `budgetEnv` (a lazy governedAI handle with SHARES.dashboard 0.2 and SHARES.site 0.2, ledgers in their own D1); the literal probe name was stale. Added dashboard/test/agent.test.mjs "a frozen budget makes the console answer without a model call" (0 AI.run calls, non-empty answer); seed/worker/test/budget.test.js already asserts both call sites.
